transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia M. (Redwood AE), Derek C. (Redwood SE), Maya P. (BrightEdge), Ethan L. (BrightEdge), Laura K. (BrightEdge PM)

Summary (auto):
- Quick sync on KV/prefix cache hit rates and pilot tuning.
- Reviewed recent benchmark numbers; hit rate up vs last week but still below target.
- Agreed on next steps: run warmup benchmark, share logs for replay, adjust prompt reuse strategy, tighten TTL and eviction policy.

Topics: cache hit rates, prefix extraction, prompt reuse hashing, LRU vs LFU eviction, warmup strategies, benchmark artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Alright everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya (BrightEdge): Hey, Maya here.
[00:12] Ethan (BrightEdge): Ethan.
[00:14] Laura (BrightEdge): Laura on.
[00:15] Derek (Redwood): Derek from Redwood, here.
[00:18] Sofia (Redwood): Cool. Agenda: Derek will walk through latest cache numbers, then we'll discuss prompt reuse strategy and next steps.
[00:25] Derek (Redwood): Okay, slide 1  


 sorry, no slides, but numbers. Last week's observed KV cache hit rate for the pilot was 42% overall, up from ~35% two weeks ago. That is aggregated across the three routes you have  

— chat, completion and rerank.
[00:40] Maya (BrightEdge): 42, nice  

 What's the target we set? 60, right?
[00:44] Derek (Redwood): Yep target is 60% for meaningful cost savings. We hit about 52% on the chat-heavy route but only 28% on the rerank route. The rerank traffic is low reuse  

 prompts change a lot.
[01:05] Ethan (BrightEdge): For rerank we do dynamic context sometimes, so makes sense. Are these prefix cache numbers or full KV cache?
[01:12] Derek (Redwood): These are KV cache hits  

 i.e., cached past KV layers when the prefix tokens align. We also looked at prefix-only caching (prefix hashing) which gave slightly different numbers: prefix hit ~48% aggregated. There's some mismatch because prompt normalization wasn't applied consistently in the client.
[01:28] Maya (BrightEdge): Ah right, our clients still send user name tokens in the system prompt in some flows; we can strip those.
[01:34] Laura (BrightEdge): We can get that fixed, but question  

 what's the TTL policy doing now? Are we evicting too aggressively?
[01:39] Derek (Redwood): Good question. Current pilot TTL is 10 minutes for hot keys, 4 hours for session keys. Eviction is LRU with an MRU bias on the GPU-side cache. For these rerank flows, short TTL is killing reuse because they run once, then get evicted before repeats show up.
[01:56] Maya (BrightEdge): Would increasing TTL to 24 hours be safe for memory/cost?
[02:01] Derek (Redwood): Memory pressure on GPU is the limiter. We can increase TTL if we tighten which prefixes we cache  

 better prefix extraction and prompt hashing to reduce unique keys. So combination: more aggressive normalization + longer TTL for canonical prefixes.
[02:18] Sofia (Redwood): Also we should consider warmup  

 pre-warming popular context from replay of last 48h traffic. That bumps observed hit rate in our benchmarks.
[02:27] Ethan (BrightEdge): We can provide logs for that. We'll need guidance on format.
[02:31] Derek (Redwood): CSV with columns: route, timestamp, prompt_text, user_id (optional), session_id. We'll share a template. Note: don't include PII fields in the prompt text; mask or replace.
[02:42] Maya (BrightEdge): Got it.
[02:44] Derek (Redwood): On prompt reuse strategy  

 we recommend canonicalization: strip ephemeral fields, normalize dates/names, and apply stable prompt templates. Then compute prefix hash (sha1 in our pipeline) to map requests to same cache key. We saw about 6% uplift just from canonicalization in a similar customer.
[03:03] Laura (BrightEdge): For us, the main complexity is product embeddings appended to prompts in rerank  

 those change slightly each request. Can we do partial prefix matching?
[03:12] Derek (Redwood): We do prefix similarity heuristics, yes. There are two options: 1) break prompt into static system+instruction prefix vs dynamic user payload and only cache static part; or 2) do fuzzy prefix grouping with configurable tolerance. Option 1 is simplest and most deterministic.
[03:29] Maya (BrightEdge): We like option 1. We'll try to move all dynamic bits after a clear delimiter.
[03:34] Derek (Redwood): Great. Implementation detail: if you move dynamic parts after '\n--DYNAMIC--\n' we can split server-side and only hash the left piece.
[03:43] Ethan (BrightEdge): Perfect.
[03:45] Sofia (Redwood): Quick note on metrics: Derek, can you share per-route token-level cost delta after caching changes?
[03:51] Derek (Redwood): Yes, we'll add per-token cost and latency breakdown. Early numbers show latency improved by ~30ms median on cached requests. Token cost drop depends on hit rate  

 at 60% we'd expect roughly 25-30% token cost reduction for the affected routes.
[04:10] Laura (BrightEdge): Any concerns around security? KMS or plaintext keys in cache?
[04:14] Derek (Redwood): Cache keys are hashed and the payload KV is stored encrypted at rest. For Private/VPC pilots we can use your KMS and HSM flow. We'll include the SOC2 sec appendix in the follow-up.
[04:25] Maya (BrightEdge): Sounds good. Also noted earlier we had some mis-attributed speaker lines in last transcript  

 minor but FYI.
[04:31] Sofia (Redwood): Noted. Transcripts can be fuzzy.
[04:34] Derek (Redwood): Operational items: I recommend three parallel actions this week: 1) BrightEdge normalize prompts / add delimiter for dynamic payloads, 2) Redwood run a warmup benchmark with current 48h replay to produce a CSV of expected hit rate uplift, 3) adjust TTLs for canonical prefixes from 10m to 4h and monitor.
[05:00] Maya (BrightEdge): We'll start on normalization; I'll get Ethan to pull logs.
[05:05] Ethan (BrightEdge): I'll target export by Friday.
[05:08] Derek (Redwood): For the benchmark, we used the internal harness  

 results link: https://redwood.example.com/poc/brightedge/caching-benchmarks (will share CSV). Note sometimes the link is long, apis, or restricted; we'll drop a copy in the shared drive.
[05:22] Laura (BrightEdge): In terms of acceptance criteria for the pilot: we want stable hit rates >55% on chat, and >40% on rerank with no user-visible latency regression.
[05:32] Sofia (Redwood): That sounds reasonable; we'll aim for that.
[05:35] Derek (Redwood): A few more caveats: prefix hashing depends on consistent tokenization  

 if you switch tokenizer or truncate differently, keys diverge. We'll provide a tokenization check script.
[05:47] Maya (BrightEdge): Good to know.
[05:50] Derek (Redwood): Also, be aware of cold-starts; we recommend always having a small warm pool of hot prefixes on dedicated capacity or pre-warm steps before bulk campaign runs.
[06:02] Laura (BrightEdge): Ok. Any blockers for sharing security docs?
[06:05] Sofia (Redwood): No blockers. I'll send SOC2 + ISO summary and KMS integration notes.
[06:10] Derek (Redwood): Last thing  

 on competitor mention, some teams ask about Anthropic / OpenAI managed offerings; the tradeoffs are similar: hosted simplicity vs dedicated/private control. For you, because of compliance, Private/VPC looks likely later.
[06:26] Ethan (BrightEdge): We are leaning that way.
[06:28] Sofia (Redwood): Great. Quick recap of next steps: Derek runs warmup benchmark and shares CSV; Maya/Ethan export logs; Sofia sends security appendix and pricing. We'll reconvene next Tuesday same time to review benchmark.
[06:46] Laura (BrightEdge): Thanks everyone.
[06:48] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks. Bye.
